title: The $q$-Collatz conjecture: Skein-module crossing resolution
html:
Conjecture. The q-Collatz conjecture: Skein-module crossing resolution

Conjecture (q-Collatz, within a QOU). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q \in \mathbb{G}_m^{\mathrm{nt}}(k) (torsion avoidance), and let \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] be the Skein module of its Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p = (S^3 \to S^2, \xi_q) (Reeb bundle). This is a statement about the q-deformed Skein dynamics of the QOU — not a claim about the classical Collatz problem, which it recovers only in the archimedean limit q \to 1, and only when the substrate admits a well-defined standard part.

We use the combinatorial q-integer [n]_q = (q^n - 1)/(q - 1), giving [2]_q = q + 1 and [3]_q = q^2 + q + 1. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra convention [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) differs by a factor of q^{(n-1)/2}. The combinatorial convention ensures the Skein divisibility identity [3]_q = q[2]_q + 1 and the contraction gap [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q.

An element P \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] is q-even if [2]_q \mid P and q-odd if [2]_q \mid (P + 1). At q = 1, we recover integer parity ([2]_1 = 2).

Unlike the integers — where every element is even or odd — a Laurent polynomial need be neither: P is q-even iff P(-1) = 0 and q-odd iff P(-1) = -1 (evaluating modulo [2]_q, i.e. at q = -1), so \mathcal{C}_q is a partial map, undefined when P(-1) \notin \{0, -1\}. Moreover this domain is not forward-invariant: almost every positive element leaves it within a few steps. Accordingly the positive cone below is the domain-stable cone — the elements whose entire forward orbit remains q-even-or-q-odd — a feature with no classical analog.

Define the Skein-Collatz map \mathcal{C}_q \colon \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] \to \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] by:

\mathcal{C}_q(P) =
\begin{cases}
  P / [2]_q & P \text{ is } q\text{-even},\\[4pt]
  \bigl([3]_q P + 1\bigr) / [2]_q & P \text{ is } q\text{-odd}.
\end{cases}

The odd branch is well-defined by the Skein divisibility identity:

[3]_q = q[2]_q + 1.

Since P is q-odd ([2]_q \mid P + 1), the numerator is divisible by [2]_q. Writing P + 1 = [2]_q Q:

\mathcal{C}_q(P) = qP + Q = [3]_q Q - q.

At q = 1, \mathcal{C}_1(n) = n/2 (even) or (3n+1)/2 (odd), recovering the Syracuse map.

Each application of \mathcal{C}_q corresponds to a crossing resolution in the Skein module (skein generation):

  • Even branch (P/[2]_q): Markov destabilization removes one strand from the braid closure, dividing the Jones polynomial by the Markov parameter. This is the q-analog of "halving."
  • Odd branch (([3]_q P + 1)/[2]_q): The Hecke relation T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1 reduces a quadratic crossing word to linear, followed by destabilization.

The Skein relation qL_+ - q^{-1}L_- = (q - q^{-1})L_0 ensures each resolution step is a convex combination:

J(L_+) = q^{-2}J(L_-) + (1 - q^{-2})J(L_0).

For q > 1, both coefficients are positive and sum to 1. The crossing resolution is non-expansive on the Jones polynomial.

The algebraic identity [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q controls the contraction. Over one Collatz cycle (one odd step followed by enough even steps to exhaust [2]_q-divisibility):

  • The odd step maps P \mapsto [3]_q Q - q. The ratio |P|/|Q| \approx [2]_q.
  • Subsequent even steps divide by [2]_q.

If each tripling is followed by at least two halvings on average, the orbit contracts. Two halvings multiply by 1/[2]_q^2; one tripling multiplies by [3]_q/[2]_q. The net factor per cycle is [3]_q / [2]_q^3 < 1, with margin:

[2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q.

Two halvings beat one tripling by a factor [2]_q^2 / [3]_q = 1 + q/[3]_q \approx 4/3.

Conjecture. Given the QOU above, for all q > 1 and all P \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]_{>0} the orbit \{\mathcal{C}_q^k(P)\}_{k \geq 0} reaches the fundamental 2-cycle \{q^{-1},\, 1 + q^{-1}\}.

At the Skein level the attractor is this 2-cycle, not the literal unknot polynomial 1: since 1 evaluates to 1 \notin \{0, -1\} modulo [2]_q (i.e. at q = -1), it is neither q-even nor q-odd, so \mathcal{C}_q(1) is undefined. The cycle \{q^{-1}, 1 + q^{-1}\} is the q-lift of the classical \{1, 2\}; writing the classical target as "1" is the q \to 1 shorthand.

The Collatz obstruction \kappa_C := \mathrm{res}_{C_q}(\kappa_0) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}_{C_q}, \mathbb{G}_m) (classical limit obstruction, QOU obstruction reduction) measures the failure of Skein-Collatz orbits to converge. One direction is safe: convergence of every orbit forces \kappa_C = 0. The converse — that \kappa_C = 0 suffices for convergence — is not established, and the Lean carrier is explicit that it is not claimed (collatz_obstruction_link.lean links \kappa_C only to the Kummer-removability leg, a divisibility fact about \chi(A)).

Why the converse cannot be cheap (the genericity caveat). The caveat recorded on the \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} leg applies here too, and is stated now so it is not rediscovered. Two steps:

  1. Vanishing at a given Kummer level is a divisibility fact, not a dynamical one. By QOU obstruction reduction(c) the obstruction vanishes at level n exactly when n \mid \chi(A); at \chi(A) = -6 the even-branch level n = 2 therefore vanishes, and this is proved outright (collatz_obstruction_link.lean) without settling any orbit. The set of levels at which it persists is cofinite by elementary arithmetic — only n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\} divide -6. (The analogous statement for the substrate parameter q, that a nonzero polynomial obstruction has cofinite non-vanishing locus, is ObstructionGenericity, sorry-free; it is a parallel fact over a different index set, not the same one.) Cheapness of this kind cannot by itself discharge an equivalence with a hard uniform statement without collapsing the equivalence — a scope-(a) objection to the route as stated, not a proof that no such equivalence holds.
  2. The content does not live in the ideal. By Reeb-flow Turing-completeness the halting set is undecidable, hence not cut out by any ideal (one length filtration, three problems). Note carefully what this does not say: it bars an ideal-theoretic description of the halting set, and it does not bar a scalar equivalent to the single proposition "every orbit converges" — such a scalar exists trivially, since any proposition is equivalent to itself (SkeinCounterfactual). Conflating the two is a recurring error, and this sentence carried it until 2026-08-15. What the undecidability does establish is that the content cannot be recovered from the ideal, so it sits in the filtration. This is structurally analogous to — not an instance of — the algebrization barrier [aaronsonwigderson2009] and the algebraic-natural-proofs barrier [grochow2017]; the shared moral is that a technique insensitive to the hard structure cannot separate, not any formal content of those theorems, which concern proof techniques in Boolean complexity and say nothing about Collatz [razborovrudich1997].

The conjecture's content therefore sits in the descent measure on the filtration, not in the vanishing of \kappa_C. Compare the same caveat on the \mathrm{P} versus \mathrm{NP} leg (\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} at non-torsion q) and on the Navier--Stokes leg (Kummer specialisation).

The shared class transfers nothing between legs. Because level-2 vanishing holds on this leg while the resolution-tree restriction is non-zero at the strictly non-torsion q_0 (\mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} at non-torsion q), the several restrictions of \kappa_0 carry different verdicts simultaneously. Identifying them would force this conjecture and \mathrm{P} \neq \mathrm{NP} to be incompatible; that identification is refuted by the pair just described (ObstructionVerdictCap). The class is shared; the verdicts are not.

Shared substrate. Convergence is the descent leg of the shared length-filtration trichotomy on \mathcal{S}(q) (one length filtration, three problems): q-Collatz asks the crossing-number filtration \ell to descend to the normal form, while \mathrm{P} vs \mathrm{NP} asks reachability within a polynomial \ell-budget and q-Navier--Stokes asks \ell to stay bounded. The three legs are three predicates on one shared object, QOU.Information.SkeinObservationSystem (this convergence question is Halts / halts_of_len_descent).
